proposal.title: Vybraxqua: a shared fuzzing service for small projects
proposal.summary: Vybraxqua builds a shared fuzzing service for small projects for maintainers of parsers and codecs.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Small projects cannot afford continuous fuzzing. Maintainers of parsers and codecs depend on fuzzing infrastructure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a shared fuzzing service for small projects called Vybraxqua. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Fuzzing infrastructure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/vybraxqua/vybraxqua-next, which 263 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on fuzzing infrastructure for 12 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/vybraxqua/vybraxqua-next. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 8 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 8.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 51800.00 EUR for 81 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Small projects cannot afford continuous fuzzing. Maintainers of parsers and codecs depend on fuzzing infrastructure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a shared fuzzing service for small projects called Vybraxqua. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Fuzzing infrastructure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/vybraxqua/vybraxqua-next, which 263 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on fuzzing infrastructure for 12 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/vybraxqua/vybraxqua-next. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 8 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 8.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 51800.00 EUR for 81 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
